name: RizzPay for WooCommerce: High-Risk & Crypto Payment Gateway
author: RizzPay

sections.description:
Payments for the stores banks keep saying no to

Most payment processors were not built for what you sell. If your WooCommerce store moves CBD, hemp, peptides, supplements, or anything a bank quietly files under high-risk, you have probably lost an account with no warning, or watched part of your revenue sit frozen in a reserve for half a year.

RizzPay is a payment gateway for WooCommerce that runs on different rails. Customers pay with cards, bank transfers, local wallets, and crypto, with more than 180 methods available at checkout. When customers pay in crypto, the money lands in USDC, a dollar-pegged stablecoin, in a wallet you control. Nothing sits on a processor’s books waiting for someone to release it.

What you get

  • Global rails: More than 180 payment methods at checkout, so a declined card or an unsupported wallet stops costing you the sale.
  • Control: Crypto payments settle in USDC to your own wallet. You hold the money, not a middleman.
  • Fast installation: Connect a wallet and start taking payments instead of waiting weeks on underwriting.
  • Final crypto settlement: Settled USDC payments do not charge back, so you are not shipping against crypto funds that vanish a month later. Cards and other fiat methods still follow their own networks’ rules.

Built for high-risk verticals

If a mainstream processor has already turned you down, this is for you. RizzPay handles payments for stores in CBD and hemp, peptides and research compounds, supplements and nutraceuticals, and other categories that keep getting labelled high-risk and shown the door. As a high-risk payment gateway that settles crypto payments in stablecoin, it gives those stores a way to get paid that does not hang on a bank’s appetite for the category this quarter.

Crypto and stablecoin payments, in plain terms

USDC is a dollar-pegged stablecoin. One coin is meant to hold the value of one US dollar, so taking payment in it is closer to getting paid in dollars than in something that swings overnight. RizzPay routes the crypto side of checkout into USDC and sends it to your wallet, so you can accept crypto payments on WooCommerce without watching exchange rates all day.

Support

For technical and merchant support, use the RizzPay Telegram channel:

https://t.me/rizzpay_io
sections.installation:
Setup takes a few minutes and happens inside your normal WooCommerce settings. You will need a RizzPay account and a USDC wallet to receive funds.

  1. In your WordPress admin, open Plugins, then Add New. Search for RizzPay for WooCommerce and click Install Now. You can also upload the plugin ZIP under Add New, then Upload Plugin.
  2. Click Activate.
  3. Go to WooCommerce, then Settings, then Payments, and find RizzPay in the list.
  4. Click Set up, enter your RizzPay API key, and connect your USDC wallet. Your API key is in your RizzPay dashboard at rizzpay.io.
  5. Choose which payment methods to show at checkout, turn RizzPay on, and save changes.
  6. Place a small test order to check the flow from end to end, then you are live.

Requirements: a current version of WordPress and WooCommerce, and PHP 7.4 or later. Your server needs to make outbound network requests, so make sure the php-curl extension is enabled.
sections.faq:
What do I get paid in?

USDC, a dollar-pegged stablecoin. Customers can pay in it directly, and the crypto side of any payment settles to you in USDC.

Do my customers need crypto to buy from me?

No. They can pay with cards, bank transfers, and local wallets as usual. Crypto is one more option at checkout, not the only one.

What does it cost?

Pricing is set by the RizzPay service and listed at rizzpay.io. There is no charge to install the plugin.

Will it work with my theme and the latest WooCommerce?

Yes. It supports current WooCommerce, including High-Performance Order Storage and the block-based checkout.

Does this plugin make my store legally compliant?

No. RizzPay is a payment service, and this plugin is the bridge between it and your store. It helps you take payments. It does not make your store compliant with the law on its own; that responsibility stays with you.
sections.changelog:
0.1.4

  • Updated WordPress.org listing copy, author metadata, tags, support links, banner artwork, and screenshot order.

0.1.3

  • Cleared remaining WordPress Plugin Check warnings for settings routing, WooCommerce save-button detection, webhook signature header handling, and intentional order-meta lookup.

0.1.2

  • Removed explicit WordPress.org translation loader because WordPress 4.6+ loads directory-hosted translations automatically.
  • Sanitized and validated webhook request method and signature header values before use.
  • Stopped storing raw signed webhook request bodies; order metadata now stores a sanitized normalized JSON snapshot.

0.1.1

  • Added trusted returnUrl handoff support for Woo checkout-created payments so payers can return to the merchant order-received page after hosted checkout.
  • Improved underpaid result messaging on hosted checkout status pages by showing actual received amount instead of requested amount.
  • Removed non-functional underpaid action buttons to keep the underpaid flow clear and deterministic.
  • Added merchant integration docs coverage for return URL behavior across API, iframe, and Woo flows.

0.1.0

  • Initial production candidate release.
  • Hosted checkout redirect + credential validation.
  • Signed webhook handling and duplicate-event protection.
  • Settled/underpaid order status mapping.
  • Checkout and provider-list UI polish.
